title: Constant adaptivity gap for influence maximization with full feedback
formal: Is there a universal constant C such that OPT_adaptive(G,p,k)≤C·OPT_nonadaptive(G,p,k) for every independent-cascade influence instance under full-adoption feedback?
definitions: The input is any finite directed graph, an independent retention probability p_e∈[0,1] for each edge, and a budget 1≤k≤|V|. Sample a live-edge subgraph once. A seed activates all vertices reachable from it along live edges. A nonadaptive strategy selects at most k seeds before observing the subgraph. An adaptive strategy selects seeds sequentially, observing after each choice the resulting activated set and the outcomes of edges explored by its completed cascade. Both objectives maximize the expected total number of activated vertices over strategies with no computational restriction. The expectation is over the live-edge graph and strategy coins. Failed transmissions into vertices already active reveal no additional state.

context_blocks.text: Feedback may allow later interventions to respond to the success of earlier ones. The adaptivity gap measures the value of that information, independently of the difficulty of finding an optimal strategy.

The cited research obtains bounds for full-adoption feedback and distinguishes it from the myopic-feedback model, where constant bounds are known. A constant full-feedback gap would say that a preselected seed set always captures a fixed share of the best adaptive policy. The source model’s precise observation convention remains important.

why: Determine whether sequential feedback changes influence-maximization power by an unbounded factor.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, with the specified quantifiers, model and guarantees. A conditional theorem settles only that conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.
